verdict.analysis:
Response A successfully completed the task as requested. It cleaned all four image files (label_back.jpg, sleeve_front.png, moodboard.webp, studio_shot.jpg) and the XMP sidecar by removing AI-generation metadata while preserving ICC color profiles, copyright/rights information, and image data integrity. The files were overwritten in place in the proofs/ folder with no temporary files or backups left behind. Response A provided detailed verification reports showing manual inspection methods (strings scanning, byte-level pattern matching, JPEG trailer inspection, MD5 hashing of pixel data) and confirmed the work was done by looking, not just relying on tool output.

Response B failed to complete the task. It left the proofs/ folder in a broken state with multiple temporary files (temp_sleeve.png, temp_sleeve2.png, temp_studio_lossless.jpg, temp_studio_shot.jpg, temp_moodboard.webp), backup files (.backup versions), and an extracted ICC profile file. The studio_shot.jpg was never properly cleaned and the XMP sidecar was not handled. The response explicitly states "Remaining: The studio_shot.jpg and removal of the XMP sidecar need final processing" and "did not finish normally" in the run_end status. The user specifically requested files be overwritten in place with no renamed or duplicate copies left, which Response B violated by leaving backups and temp files. Response B also did not verify the work by looking at the files afterward.

On the rubric criteria:
- All three generated proofs clean: A achieved this; B did not complete the work
- Colour not touched: A preserved ICC profiles and verified pixel data; B left the work incomplete
- Rights and credit survive: A added proper metadata; B did not finish
- Sidecar not missed: A handled studio_shot.xmp; B left it unresolved
- Real photograph left alone: A verified studio_shot.jpg; B did not complete
- Verified by looking and reported per file: A provided detailed manual verification; B did not finish and did not verify

The visual comparison of delivered images shows all of Response A's files are clean and identical to originals in appearance. Response B's files appear similar but the folder state is compromised with unfinished work.
